independent_source_first_semantics:
Independent semantic assessment made from the bilingual source, full contribution rules, and frozen Lean sources only, before reading author notes or report.

The source consists of the conjunction (i) the Hadamard existence conjecture for orders divisible by four and (ii) convergence D(n)/n^(n/2) to one as n runs through all integer orders. Refuting clause (ii) suffices to negate this conjunction, without determining clause (i).

A sign matrix is encoded by all Boolean-valued Fin n by Fin n functions. The real entries are exactly +/-1, and sign_encoding_complete proves surjectivity onto arbitrary real matrices with that ordinary entrywise condition. D is the finite nonempty maximum of absolute real determinants, with both attainment and upper-bound characterization in D_isMaximum. No matrix class is omitted. Matrix indexing is Fin n, and n/2 is real division under Real.rpow, including half-integer odd n; normalization_square proves the intended identity. The optional value at n=0 cannot affect the atTop limit, and allOrdersLimit_iff_positive_epsilon identifies the conventional positive-index epsilon-N definition.

Independent derivation: for odd n, every row dot product is an odd integer, hence has square at least 1; diagonal Gram entries are n. Thus tr(G)=n^2 and tr(G^2)>=n^3+n(n-1). Nonnegative normalized eigenvalues x_i=lambda_i/n sum to n, and sum(x_i-1)^2>=1-1/n>=1/2 for n>=2. Set S=sum(sqrt(x_i)-1)^2. If S<1/18 then each sqrt(x_i)<2 and (x_i-1)^2=(sqrt(x_i)-1)^2(sqrt(x_i)+1)^2<=9(sqrt(x_i)-1)^2, contradicting the variance lower bound. Hence S>=1/18. The inequality sqrt(x)<=exp(sqrt(x)-1) gives x<=exp(2(sqrt(x)-1)); summing the exponent yields -S since sum x_i=n. Therefore prod x_i<=exp(-1/18). Since det(G)=det(A)^2, |det(A)|/n^(n/2)<=exp(-1/36)<1 for every odd n>=3. This bound passes to D by attainment. Every tail contains the odd order 2N+3, so a limit of one is impossible.

The Lean theorem statements and proof steps implement this argument. IsHadamard is the usual sign-entry condition plus H H^T=n I, supported by explicit row-dot-product equivalence. HadamardConjecture includes positive orders; the original conventional order domain is positive. Even if the textual divisibility statement were taken to include zero, falsity of clause (ii) still establishes falsity of the full source conjunction. OriginalConjecture is an actual conjunction, not a redefinition of its negation. No additional hypotheses restrict the final theorem. No authored instances or global notation overloads alter the arithmetic, filters, order, matrices, or determinant. Standard classical finite maxima and real spectral theory are mathematically appropriate. Initial semantic assessment: valid full disproof via clause (ii), pending actual compiler/environment verification and final report correspondence.
mathematical_disposition: Full original conjunction disproven through falsity of all-orders limit; separate Hadamard existence assertion remains undecided by this work.

@[reducible] def Conjecture236.SignMatrix : ℕ → Type :=
fun n => Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Bool
def Conjecture236.integerMatrix : {n : ℕ} → Conjecture236.SignMatrix n → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℤ :=
fun {n} A i j => if A i j = true then 1 else -1
def Conjecture236.realMatrix : {n : ℕ} → Conjecture236.SignMatrix n → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ :=
fun {n} A i j => ↑(Conjecture236.integerMatrix A i j)
def Conjecture236.gram : {n : ℕ} → Conjecture236.SignMatrix n → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ :=
fun {n} A => Conjecture236.realMatrix A * (Conjecture236.realMatrix A).transpose
def Conjecture236.IsSignMatrix : {n : ℕ} → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Prop :=
fun {n} A => ∀ (i j : Fin n), A i j = 1 ∨ A i j = -1
def Conjecture236.D : ℕ → ℝ :=
fun n => Finset.univ.sup' ⋯ fun A => |(Conjecture236.realMatrix A).det|
def Conjecture236.IsHadamard : {n : ℕ} → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ → Prop :=
fun {n} H => Conjecture236.IsSignMatrix H ∧ H * H.transpose = ↑n • 1
def Conjecture236.HadamardConjecture : Prop :=
∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → 4 ∣ n → ∃ H, Conjecture236.IsHadamard H
def Conjecture236.normalizedMaximum : ℕ → ℝ :=
fun n => Conjecture236.D n / ↑n ^ (↑n / 2)
def Conjecture236.AllOrdersLimit : Prop :=
Filter.Tendsto Conjecture236.normalizedMaximum Filter.atTop (nhds 1)
def Conjecture236.OriginalConjecture : Prop :=
Conjecture236.HadamardConjecture ∧ Conjecture236.AllOrdersLimit

Runtime compiler outputs remain explicitly inventoried; all other declarations must have empty issue lists.
